title: Point GitHub Pages at /docs and drop the root redirect
detail: Pages is live and serving main, but its source path is the repository root, and changing it needs repository admin rights that this branch's automation does not have. The workaround in place is a root index.html that redirects to docs/index.html plus a root .nojekyll, so the canonical URL works today and nothing is duplicated - the redirect cannot go stale because every page, stylesheet and JSON file is served from under docs/. The remaining step for an admin is Settings -> Pages -> source: main, /docs, after which the root index.html and root .nojekyll can be deleted. Publishing the whole root also means memory/, data/ and the sources are downloadable from the Pages URL; that is no new exposure for a public repository, but /docs would serve only the site.
where: repository Settings -> Pages (admin only) - index.html and .nojekyll at the repo root are the current workaround

title: Minute-bar intraday engine
detail: Expose multiple decision points per session on top of the existing intraday path, keep the order book alive across them, and add a closing-auction order type. This is what makes @GapAndGo_YOLO, @OvernightCarry_NO and @SpreadHarvester_MM measurable instead of caveated (L-03, IR-08).

title: Real event data: earnings calendar, EPS surprises, short interest
detail: Replaces the price/volume proxies behind @DriftRider_PEAD and @SqueezeHunter_TF (IR-07) and lets the post-mortems attribute returns to identifiable events rather than to statistical drift. FINRA publishes short interest twice monthly; earnings dates are available from several vendors. Dividend and ex-date schedules belong here too: for 15 of the 17 instruments the ex-dates and per-share amounts are declared scenario parameters, not observations, and IR-31 showed that the accounting around them is where a season's short-side returns actually move. A real schedule would also let the ex-date price drop be checked against the tape instead of assumed.
effort: a week

title: Formal significance testing on the results
detail: Bootstrap confidence intervals for Sharpe, alpha and max drawdown; a Deflated Sharpe Ratio to account for having run twenty strategies; and a cross-scenario test of whether the winner's rank is distinguishable from chance. Right now the robustness panel shows the spread but does not test it (L-08).
effort: a few days

title: Multi-season support and a season archive
detail: Season 1 is hard-coded into config constants and the site copy. Generalising it needs a season registry, per-season memory namespaces, and an archive page that compares winners across seasons - which is also how the project would accumulate the many independent years that L-08 asks for.
effort: a week

title: Financing curve: interest on cash and a margin debit rate
detail: Removes the zero-risk-free-rate simplification (L-06). Accrue daily in Account.accrue_carry against a declared SOFR or T-bill series plus a spread, and subtract the same rate in the Sharpe numerator so the ratio stays internally consistent.
effort: a day

title: Publish a venue-parameter sensitivity harness (the IR-29 answer)

IR-29 shows a half-tick change moved one participant 28.3pp, so a single-path ranking is not a skill ordering; this harness is what would turn that from a caveat into a measurement, and it would also settle the square-root vs 3/5-power impact question empirically inside the model rather than only citing the literature.
where: sim/cli.py (a new 'sensitivity' subcommand) - analytics.robustness_panel is the template; publish as robustness.html plus assets/data/sensitivity.json
effort: a day; each full six-scenario run is about 14 seconds, so a 12-perturbation grid is a few minutes of compute

title: Cite-hygiene job for the source register (networked, not in CI by design)
effort: S
detail: IR-33 found two official URLs in the register returning 404, including one cited for a fee rate, and neither was caught because nothing opens the links after they are written. The register now requires a stored artefact behind a FETCHED-VERIFIED row, which fixes the rot-forward problem but not the rot-already-there problem: a link that was live when the excerpt was taken still goes stale silently a year later. The missing piece is a scheduled job that re-opens every URL in sim/config.py's register plus the links in the three research JSON files, classifies the response, and opens an issue listing the rows that moved. It must not be a merge gate: a red build because a regulator rate-limits a bot is worse than no build, and several of these hosts (sec.gov, finra.org, federalregister.gov) block unauthenticated automation intermittently. So it belongs in a weekly scheduled workflow with continue-on-error, reporting per-URL status, and the manual sweep recorded in VERIFICATION_LOG.md remains the backstop.
where: new .github/workflows/cite-hygiene.yml; scripts/check_links.py with a fetch classifier that separates 404/410 (broken) from 403/429/timeout (blocked, needs a human)

The venue is right to refuse; the rules should instead aim at the first session on or after the issue date, which is what a participant who reads the announcement would do.
